description: Value-codec conformance vectors (docs/spec/multi-language.md). Each case is a Lua and/or JavaScript expression; the value it yields crosses the codec once. 'typed' is the expected value in the rendering below, 'error' the codec's refusal message, 'accepted' a value that must cross without its rendering being compared. 'viaJs' is the rendering after a further trip through JavaScript when it differs from 'typed'. 'luaVersions' limits a case to those Lua versions; 'guest': false marks a value resource code cannot build (tested at the codec level only).
rendering: nil | true | false | i:<integer> | f:<float, shortest round-trip, exponent in lower case> | "<string, with \" \\ and bytes below 0x20 escaped as \\u00xx>" | [v,...] for an empty table or keys exactly 1..n | {k=v,...} otherwise, integer keys (i:<n>) ascending then string keys (quoted) in byte order
consumers: sdk/dotnet/ScriptGo.Host.Tests/CodecVectorTests.cs (.NET kit: KeraLua and Jint guests, and each crossing the other)

cases.name: js_integral_number
cases.note: JavaScript has one number type: an integral value within ±2^53 crosses as an integer

cases.name: js_beyond_safe_integer
cases.note: beyond ±2^53 an integral JavaScript number stays a float

cases.name: lua_max_integer
cases.note: JavaScript numbers are doubles: a 64-bit integer beyond ±2^53 comes back as a float

cases.name: js_empty_object
cases.note: an empty table has no shape; JavaScript receives []

cases.name: js_canonical_integer_keys
cases.note: only canonical integer strings become integer keys

cases.name: lua_integer_and_string_key
cases.note: a JavaScript object cannot hold both keys: the string key, written last, wins, and the table comes back as a sequence

cases.name: shared_not_cyclic
cases.lua: (function() local s = { 1 } return { a = s, b = s } end)()
cases.js: (() => { const s = [1]; return { a: s, b: s }; })()
cases.note: a table reached twice is copied twice

cases.name: js_array_named_properties_ignored
cases.note: only the indices of an array are read

cases.name: depth_32
cases.lua: (function() local v = 1 for _ = 1, 32 do v = { v } end return v end)()
cases.js: (() => { let v = 1; for (let i = 0; i < 32; i++) v = [v]; return v; })()

cases.name: too_deep
cases.lua: (function() local v = 1 for _ = 1, 33 do v = { v } end return v end)()
cases.js: (() => { let v = 1; for (let i = 0; i < 33; i++) v = [v]; return v; })()

cases.name: cyclic
cases.lua: (function() local t = {} t.self = t return t end)()
cases.js: (() => { const o = {}; o.self = o; return o; })()

cases.name: lua_thread
cases.note: resources have no coroutine library, so only a host-level codec meets a thread

cases.name: lua_float_key
cases.error: codec: table keys must be strings or integers

cases.name: lua_boolean_key
cases.error: codec: table keys must be strings or integers

cases.name: lua_table_key
cases.error: codec: table keys must be strings or integers

cases.name: js_class_instance
cases.error: codec: cannot transfer a class instance

cases.name: js_accessor
cases.error: codec: cannot transfer an accessor property
